prompt.format: Create feature docs for this project from what is already there (README, code, documentation): docs/FEATURES.md with a short introduction and a table with one row per epic (link, topic, status), and one file per epic in docs/features/epic-XX-<slug>.md with a description, a line **Stories:**, a line **Status (date):** and stories such as **US-XXYY: Title** <status> followed by As a / in order to / I would like to, Epic, Priority, Complexity, Acceptance Criteria as checkboxes in the form Given/When/Then, Notes and Dependencies. Status markers: 📋 Planned, 🚧 In progress, ✅ Done (merged; add "Released in vX.Y.Z" when released). Order the epics by topic, not by release.
prompt.rule: Also add a project rule through AI-DLC's own way of saving rules, not by editing the memory files directly, so every AI tool in the project (Claude Code, opencode and the others) follows it: a new story the person describes goes into the right epic file right away; when work on a story starts, set it to 🚧 In progress in its status marker, the epic's **Status (…)** line and its FEATURES.md row; when it is built and approved, set it to ✅ Done and tick its met acceptance criteria; as soon as the release it goes into is known, write it out ("for vX.Y.Z", and "Released in vX.Y.Z" when the tag is cut); a delivered story never stays in progress. AI-DLC's way of saving rules only adds rules, so if the project's memory files already hold a story lifecycle rule (a line ending with a (story-lifecycle: …) tag, or an older rule about these status markers), delete that line by hand, the one direct edit allowed here, and say which line you took out. End the rule with {tag}, exactly as written, so the app can tell which rule it is.
prompt.ruleContinuous: Also add a project rule through AI-DLC's own way of saving rules, not by editing the memory files directly, so every AI tool in the project (Claude Code, opencode and the others) follows it: a new story the person describes goes into the right epic file right away; when work on a story starts, set it to 🚧 In progress in its status marker, the epic's **Status (…)** line and its FEATURES.md row; when it is built and approved, set it to ✅ Done and tick its met acceptance criteria; when it is deployed, set it to 🚀 Deployed in the same three places; a delivered story never stays in progress. AI-DLC's way of saving rules only adds rules, so if the project's memory files already hold a story lifecycle rule (a line ending with a (story-lifecycle: …) tag, or an older rule about these status markers), delete that line by hand, the one direct edit allowed here, and say which line you took out. End the rule with {tag}, exactly as written, so the app can tell which rule it is.
